slides.headline: Tummy gap after having a baby?
slides.sub: Abdominal separation is really common. Here's what usually helps.

slides.title: Common and a normal change
slides.body: Your tummy muscles stretch apart during pregnancy to make room for your baby. Most people have some separation after birth, and for many it narrows over the first few months.

slides.title: Function matters more than the gap
slides.body: The width of the gap isn't the whole story. How well your tummy muscles support you during everyday tasks often matters more than exactly how wide the gap measures.

slides.title: Start with breathing and gentle work
slides.body: Gentle breathing, pelvic floor and deep tummy exercises are usually a good starting point. Your physio can guide you on when to progress to more challenging core work.

slides.title: Everyday habits that help
slides.body: Roll onto your side to get out of bed, breathe out as you lift your baby or the pram, and try not to hold your breath when you strain. Small changes add up.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: A bulge that doesn't settle, pain around the gap, ongoing back pain, leaking, or a feeling of heaviness in the pelvic area is worth assessing with your physio or GP.
